absences: 8h simulated via ?dev=1&absent=8h after 34 min of cold play (03:53-04:27), then 21 min on return (04:27-04:48)
horizon.$detail: 14 sends watched at the slowest pace (one bailed on purpose at D3 to learn what return does); 5 deaths read (4 watched + the offline one via TRACE); 16 own edits (add/replace rows, thresholds, second conds, reorders, drops) plus 4 offered patches tapped (rest, drink unknown, the stall patch, attack boss).

criterion.delayedRecall: same-day: I had thrown out my 'foe: summoner -> attack summoner' row to make room for drink heal, and on D5 a goblin captain pinned my L4 fighter in a corridor with a stack of summoned goblins and monkeys for three flat minutes at 29/42 hp while the alert climbed to !!!. He finally got the captain, walked down through bloat gas ('-3 gas') to D7 and banked $125 at 14/42, and the report's reel said 'The air stings: bloats ahead. Banked $125.' The first thing I did back at camp was put the summoner row back above attack nearest, and the next run he killed the conjurer on sight.

$probes.return: I came back to 16 runs, +$1170 home, fighter L3, a STALL block saying 'R4 bank ended 9 runs, none past D6' with two patches, usage stats ('R2 fired 4 of 16 runs'), one offline death to read and a shelf with every identified potion; I took the depth>=6 patch, raised rest to 25%, bought supplies 3->5 and auto: restock. I would not rather have stayed: the absence levelled the fighter, which nothing I could edit in 34 minutes did.
$probes.attribution: The last run ended with 'goblin warlord . D8 . 1 hp short . gap' after my R5 attack summoner fired five times at hp 6 with five foes and my bank row said 'no way'; that was my rule order and my missing boss row, and I said so before the patch offered it.
$probes.clarity: The moment I turned R4 from attack nearest into bank the forecast flipped from 'death 100%' to 'bank 100% . death 0% . ~$62' in about a second; what I never got straight was why the same six rows read 94/6, then 79/21, then 72/28 in a row.
$probes.decisions: 'hp<50% . depth>=5 -> bank' gave D5 70% . bank 55% . death 35% . ~$54 against bank-at-50% 95/5 for the same gold: depth for risk, and I took the depth.
$probes.mastery: Death 3 taught me that bank is a walk, not an exit ('R4 bank' for seven ticks at hp 10 with two jackals adjacent), so I moved it above attack and stopped ordering it after the fight.
$probes.tension: Watching 0/38 . D4 . 'rest 20m' land on the same frame as 'OGRE WINDS UP' with $78 carried, and later 'died $0 . $234 carried' on D8, were the two times I leaned in; most bank-at-D3 runs were foregone.
$probes.feel: The forecast bars re-drawing under my finger after every chip is the best-feeling thing in it; the worst was the D5 corridor where five foes drew on one tile as one unreadable smear under 'R6 ATTACK GOBLIN'. Audio: unassessed.
$probes.surprise: 'Goblin Captain: summoner', 'bloat: gas', 'archer draws', 'thieves!', 'The green one: poison', and a warlord boss on D8 each put a row in my set; the cage/shrine/den lines repeated verbatim every run.
$probes.expression: A fighter who hits summoners and archers first, drinks heal at 30%, rests at 25% and only walks home under 40% once past D6; the game calls my heirs 'the gambler fighter' and 'the cowardly fighter' in the chronicle.
$probes.story: 'A thief snatched the sealed scroll?. D5: the Warrens. Trophy: no heal to D5. Zelak the Goblin Captain is avenged. Banked $65.' is a run I could retell; 'Took the sword +1 from the cage. D3: the Warrens. Banked $45.' is not.
$probes.pacing: In-run at the slowest pace: 6-10 callouts a minute, runs 30-100 s at L1 and 3-4 min at L4, one 3-minute flat pile-up; check-in: 2-4 min to read the reel, touch a row and send; cadence: only the overnight tested, and it yielded 16 runs because each costs a 20-minute rest.
$probes.failure: 'burst . D6 . 3 hp short . 8 unknown unused . gap' with 'R1 rest: not safe . R2 drink heal: unknown item . R3 attack summoner: not in view <- goblin captain last seen D5 (6,18)' told me everything except that my R5 bank never got a turn; the morgue's 'hazard first' did.
$probes.autonomy: I pressed bail at D3 to find out that return keeps 60% and bank 100%; nothing prompted it and the ledger showed the split.
$probes.progression: Within a run: 36 -> 42 max hp and $0 -> $286; between runs: fighter L1 -> L4, rows 4 -> 7, vault 1 -> 2, supplies 3 -> 5, star 0 -> 5, the shelf growing from 'leash $30' to every identified potion and scroll; automation: path: bones and auto: restock, both bought with marks.
$probes.aesthetic: A dark olive warren with a big red-cloaked fighter and small tan jackals, pixel-font callouts, monospace chrome; I would not sit in it doing nothing, but I never wanted to look away either.

axes.proxy: time-to-first-rule-edit; misread rate on the trace
axes.note: The rows, the per-row reasons ('not safe', 'unknown item', 'no way') and the live forecast ('bank 100% . death 0% . ~$62' one second after picking bank) made the loop clear from the first death. Lapses that kept it at adequate: the same rule set forecast 94/6, 79/21 and 72/28 across three consecutive edits (+-18-21), the forecast showed the empty set 2's 'death 100% . rat 70%' under my set after a tab switch, death 1 read as a rule gap (7 unknown unused, heal row inert) but was stamped 'dice', and an offered patch pushed me to '6/5 . drop one' with no warning.

Every check-in had a choice I could defend: bank at hp<50% (95/5, ~$61) vs 'hp<50% . depth>=5' (55/35, ~$54, D5 70%); bank above or below attack; which row to drop at 6/5 (I dropped the summoner row and a captain pile-up on D5 made me pay for it); vault weapon vs potion; marks on +1 row vs vault vs auto: restock. Named lapse: the forecast's +-20 swamps one-notch edits, so rest 20% vs 25% was a guess, and the first patch set (rest survives 100% reach ~0 vs two negatives) was a no-brainer.

Things I could not do at minute 5 and could at minute 50: order bank before attack because banking is a multi-tick walk (death 3 trace: 'R4 bank' x7 at hp 10 with 2 foes), put 'foe: ranged -> attack ranged' first (forecast D5 16% -> 96%), keep unknown-drinking as a last resort at 20%, and use conds the hero learned ('foe: gas', 'foe: telegraph', 'foe: boss' unlocked from facts). Deepest went D5 -> D8. Named lapse: from run 4 to run 9 nothing I edited moved D6 off ~10%; the wall was fighter level, which only the offline runs raised.

Stakes I chose and felt: 'hp<40% . depth>=6 -> bank' after the stall patch, then 'died $0 . $234 carried . bones: 9 items on D8'; '0/38 . D4 . rest 20m' landing over 'OGRE WINDS UP' with $78 in hand. But at bank-at-50% the forecast said 'death 5%' and the runs were foregone: banked $45 at D3, $33 at D3, $47 at D5 with nothing in doubt; the 3-minute corridor pile-up at a flat 29/42 was waiting, not sweating.

axes.proxy: death-cause entropy; distinct situations per run
axes.note: Situations that changed my configuration: 'Goblin Captain: summoner' (summoner row), 'bloat: gas' and 'ogre winds up' (retreat rows), 'goblin archer 71%' in the forecast (ranged row), 'The green one: poison. Gambled: poison potion.' (gamble moved to 20%), a warlord boss on D8 (boss row); plus thieves stealing my heal, a monkey stealing the fire potion, 'Found heir 3's bones: 9 items'. Named lapse: 'A cage: three inside, one to take.' / 'A shrine. Pray, at a price.' / 'A den. Something sleeps.' appeared in nearly every run word for word and rarely mattered.

'yours: 7 of 7 rows', the forecast tagging me 'gambler', and the chronicle naming heirs 'the gambler fighter' / 'the cowardly fighter' made the set feel mine. Kept from strong because after an hour the set is what any fighter converges on (heal 30 / rest / bank / attack) with two foe-tag rows on top; rogue, the cards and set 2 went untried, so I saw one archetype.

The reel writes runs with a turn: 'Zelak the Goblin Captain is avenged.' (my summoner row killed the captain that killed heir 1), 'Gambled: heal potion. R2 drink ? caught him. Banked $98.', 'A conjurer took him to 2 HP; no row fired; died.' My own best run has one (see delayedRecall). Named lapse: about half the reels are filler ('The cage opens: one is his. D3: the Warrens. Banked $45.').

axes.proxy: run length; check-in length; dead time at 1x
axes.note: In-run: at the slowest pace 6-10 callouts a minute; L1 runs lasted 30-100 s (too short to 'watch for minutes'), L4 runs 3-4 min; one 3-minute stretch of 'R6 . attack nearest' at a flat 29/42 was dead. Check-in: read reel, touch one row, send is 2-4 min; the return read took ~15 min and was bounded by a chosen stop. Administration: sheets with no close control (tap the dim), potions bought one tap each, '6/5 . drop one' after a patch. Cadence: only the overnight was taken (16 runs, 'rested 322m'); 20-min and 4-h absences untested, which caps this at adequate.

axes.proxy: share of deaths with a matched-rule trace
axes.note: All five deaths read had cause, margin and the rule: 'goblin warlord . D8 . 1 hp short . gap' with 'R1 drink heal: no item <- R1 drank heal at 12/42 hp', 'R4 bank: no way', 'R5 attack summoner: fired'; the offline one had 'R3 drank fire at 7/40 hp'. Recovery is one tap ('send' skips the rest). Named lapse: death 1 was stamped 'dice' although its own screen said '7 unknown unused' and 'R1 unknown item' (the preset heal row could never fire), and death 2's screen never mentioned my bank row at all; the morgue's 'hazard first' explained it.

I set my own goals (bank early for rogue, then push depth, then bail at D3 just to learn 'returned $27 . $45 carried . keeps 60%') and the vocabulary let me express them ('depth >= 5', 'seen >= 50% -> descend'); the route inside the dungeon is the hero's, and I never found a reason to write anything but the fighter's obvious set.

All three layers seen. Within-run: 36 -> 42 max hp, $0 -> $286, items and cages. Persistent: fighter L1 -> L4 ('fighter +562 . L3 ^1' overnight), star 0 -> 5, rows 4 -> 7, vault 1 -> 2, supplies 3 -> 5, class: rogue, conds unlocked by facts ('foe: gas', 'has: heal'), the shelf growing from 'leash $30' to every identified potion and scroll. Automation: path: bones ('Found heir 3's bones: 9 items'), auto: restock ('-$180 spent' on the next report). Named lapse: gold outran its sinks ($1973 at the end with a $40 potion the priciest thing I wanted), and routine runs gave 'MARKS 0'.

A dark olive warren, a big red-cloaked pixel fighter, small tan jackals and a grey ogre, callouts in a pixel face, chrome in monospace; coherent and readable at phone size, muddy in the tiles, and the pile-ups turn to mush. Audio unassessed.

axes.note: Scored same-day (the brief asked for it; anti-bias rule noted). Came back to '16 RUNS . D6 DEEPEST . 15 BANKED . 1 DEATHS . +$1170 home . +$408 salvage . rested 322m', a STALL diagnosis ('R4 bank ended 9 runs, none past D6') with two patches, 'R2 fired 4 of 16 runs' usage lines, a 5-line reel, an offline death with a full trace, fighter L3 and a shelf of identified items. Three decisions made in the first two minutes; first meaningful action within 30 s. Yield was predictable (20-min rest per run). axes.proxy: share of deaths attributable to a rule the player wrote
axes.note: Four of five deaths ended in a row I wrote or a gap I can name: my gamble row drank poison ('Gambled: poison potion.') and fire ('R3 drank fire at 7/40 hp'), my bank-after-attack order (death 2), my dropped summoner row (the D5 pile-up), my missing boss row (death 4). Wins were mine too: 'Zelak the Goblin Captain is avenged' after my summoner row, 'R1 drink heal caught him' after I re-added it. I retold the best run in the first person without trying. Named lapse: death 1 was 'dice' on preset rules, where I could see the gap (7 unknown potions, no row to drink them) but the verdict did not say so.
